description: I’m a full-stack software development student who loves building real, working applications from idea to finished product. I enjoy clean design and solving problems with code. I’m new to NASA and space science, and I’m joining this challenge to learn, explore and grow my skills while creating something I’m proud of.
summary: Last Signal is a narrated, interactive story about the machines NASA left behind on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Instead of a list of facts, it plays like a short documentary in the browser: one machine at a time, from its mission to its final silence. Using real NASA images, subtitles, music that follows the mood of each scene, and a narrator whose tone changes from celebratory to quiet, it tells the stories of the Apollo 11 descent stage, Viking 1, Spirit and Opportunity, Ingenuity, Kepler, NEAR Shoemaker and Pioneer 10. Live "silence clocks" count how long each machine has been silent. The experience opens with a question, "What happens to a machine when its mission ends?", and closes with the answer: they may look abandoned, but they are not forgotten. It makes NASA's history feel human and accessible to anyone, on any device.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Last Signal is a one-page, scroll-free story that plays like a short film. Each scene follows one NASA machine from its mission to the moment it went quiet. Real NASA images, subtitles, a narrator and music carry the story. A live "silence clock" shows how long each machine has been silent.

HOW IT WORKS

Lines appear one at a time and advance automatically or on a click. The narrator speaks faster and brighter in celebratory scenes (Sojourner, Spirit, Ingenuity) and slower and lower in sad ones (Opportunity, Pioneer 10). The background music is generated live in the browser and softens whenever the narrator speaks.

WHY IT MATTERS

People usually hear about active missions. This project gives the retired machines a human story, built on real mission facts, so audiences feel a personal connection to them and to the science they made possible.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no frameworks. Web Audio API (music), Web Speech API (narration), GitHub Pages (hosting). NASA images and mission facts from NASA mission pages.

CREATIVITY AND DESIGN CHOICES

The story opens with a question and ends with a conclusion tied to the challenge title. Images change with the narration. The tone and the music change with the emotion of each scene.

USE OF AI

AI tools helped build this project; see the Use of Super Intelligence section. Facts were checked against NASA mission pages.
